summary: Auroora Yhtiöt Oyj (AUROORA.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) owns and builds specialist businesses in electrical systems, industrial products and services, and water and environment. Its companies sell transformers, automation systems, industrial parts, technical services, and water-treatment and recycling solutions. The share price was 9.84 EUR, market capitalisation was EUR 295m and enterprise value was EUR 355m on 13 November 2026 in this Valuatum market report dated 13 November 2026. Analysts forecast company sales of EUR 267m and operating profit of EUR 13m for 2026, rising to sales of EUR 305m and operating profit of EUR 18m in 2028.

The 9.84 EUR share price is built mainly on Electrical systems, assigned 8.90 EUR per share at 25.6x 2028 operating profit, and Industrial products and services, assigned 2.90 EUR per share at 12.0x. Water and environment contributes 0.05 EUR per share at 23.3x a near-zero 2028 operating profit. The businesses total 11.85 EUR per share before debt and other claims, less cash of 2.01 EUR per share. Electrical systems represents 75% of that pre-claims amount and 59% of the split 2028 operating profit, while Industrial products and services represents 24% and 41%.

The whole company trades at 20x analysts' 2028 operating profit, compared with listed peers at about 14.5x. The difference is concentrated in Electrical systems at 25.6x versus a 17.4x peer median, while Industrial products and services is 12.0x versus 10.1x and Water and environment is 23.3x versus 17.8x. The reading depends on 2026 sales of EUR 267m, second-half adjusted operating profit of about EUR 9m, order-book conversion, margin delivery and the closing and integration of Labko and Coating Source.

thesis.title: What you pay for
thesis.text: Electrical systems receives 8.90 EUR per share, or 75% of the EUR 11.85 businesses total before claims. Industrial products and services adds 2.90 EUR, while Water and environment adds 0.05 EUR, leaving nearly all of the operating-business price with two units.

thesis.title: Above listed peers
thesis.text: Electrical systems is priced at 25.6x 2028 operating profit against a 17.4x peer median. Its 2028 margin is only 5% in the split, so the price rests on sales growth and successful delivery of a EUR 121.5m backlog rather than forecast margin expansion.

thesis.title: Second-half test
thesis.text: About EUR 9m of adjusted operating profit in the second half of 2026 would complete analysts' EUR 13m full-year forecast after about EUR 4m in the first half. Labko's expected year-end closing and Coating Source's expected November closing provide additional tests of the forecast.

valuePools.name: Electrical systems
valuePools.economics: 25.6x 2028 operating profit · EUR 10m forecast operating profit · peers 14.9x-25.6x, median 17.4x
valuePools.text: Electrical systems is the largest business, selling transformers and reactors, designing and building substations, and providing industrial electrification, automation and power-quality services to utilities and industrial companies. Outside sales were EUR 129.7m in 2025 and adjusted EBITA was EUR 8.3m, a 6.4% margin. The split assigns EUR 194m of sales and EUR 10m of operating profit in 2028, implying a 5% margin. The share price assigns 8.90 EUR per share to the business at 25.6x operating profit, the highest point in the listed peer range. The evidence supporting the sales case is a EUR 56.8m second-quarter 2026 order intake and a EUR 121.5m backlog at June 2026, up from EUR 96.9m at December 2025. The key constraint is project pricing: a 4% margin would leave the multiple further above peers.

valuePools.name: Industrial products and services
valuePools.economics: 12.0x 2028 operating profit · EUR 7m forecast operating profit · peers 10.0x-11.3x, median 10.1x
valuePools.text: Industrial products and services sells specialist industrial products and provides technical and maintenance services to manufacturers, process industries and infrastructure customers. Outside sales were EUR 57m in 2025, while the split assigns EUR 86m of sales and EUR 7m of operating profit in 2028, an 8% margin. The price assigns 2.90 EUR per share at 12.0x operating profit, above Konecranes at 10.0x, Valmet at 10.1x and Instalco at 11.3x. The premium rests on specialist acquired companies and the possibility that profit grows into the price. Segment sales grew 87.9% in 2025, while Suomen Teknohaus contributed a niche Finnish piping business with a 38-year history. Trading remains uneven: adjusted EBITA margin was 2.9% in the first quarter of 2026 and 14.6% in the second. Labko, Coating Source and BRIX Facades add further execution evidence.

valuePools.name: Water and environment
valuePools.economics: 23.3x 2028 operating profit · approximately EUR 0m forecast operating profit · peers 8.9x-23.3x, median 17.8x
valuePools.text: Water and environment sells water-treatment and circular-economy solutions and related services to industrial and municipal customers. Outside sales were EUR 16m in 2025, including Operon's operation of nine Finnish treatment plants serving wastewater equivalent to about 250,000 people. The split assigns EUR 25m of sales and approximately EUR 0m of operating profit in 2028, roughly break-even after a 2025 adjusted loss of about 1.2% on outside sales. The price assigns only 0.05 EUR per share, but that amount equates to 23.3x a near-zero profit, matching the highest peer, Pentair. A EUR 28.9m segment backlog at December 2025 and a pro forma adjusted EBITA margin of 2.3% provide possible operating leverage. Rasmix added about EUR 5.0m of 2025 revenue, while Labko could add about EUR 10.5m if it closes and is allocated to this segment.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The 9.84 EUR share price is predominantly a claim on two operating businesses rather than on separately identified forests or property. Electrical systems contributes 8.90 EUR per share, Industrial products and services contributes 2.90 EUR, and Water and environment contributes 0.05 EUR. Together the businesses amount to 11.85 EUR per share before debt and other claims, less cash of 2.01 EUR per share. Electrical systems supplies 59% of the split 2028 operating profit, or EUR 10m, from EUR 194m of sales at a 5% margin. Industrial products and services supplies 41%, or EUR 7m, from EUR 86m at an 8% margin. Water and environment contributes approximately EUR 0m from EUR 25m at roughly break-even. The whole-company calculation is 20x analysts' 2028 operating profit of EUR 18m, while the 2026 measure is 27x analysts' EUR 13m. The structure therefore depends on forecast operating profit arriving across the two larger businesses, with the Electrical systems order book providing the clearest sales evidence. Because its assigned profit is only EUR 10m, modest margin variation has a material effect on the multiple represented by the share price.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price is above peers
coreAnalysis.text: The peer comparison is driven by the denominator as much as by the business descriptions. Electrical systems is priced at 25.6x 2028 operating profit, against a peer median of 17.4x and a range of 14.9x to 25.6x. Its assigned margin falls from 6.4% adjusted EBITA in 2025 to 5% operating profit in 2028, so the price is not explained by forecast margin improvement. Instead, the EUR 121.5m backlog and EUR 56.8m second-quarter 2026 order intake support the sales increase required to reach EUR 194m. Industrial products and services is priced at 12.0x against a 10.1x median, despite the split margin falling from 11.0% adjusted EBITA to 8% operating profit. Acquisitions such as Heatmasters and Suomen Teknohaus provide the specialist-company rationale, but quarterly margins of 2.9% and 14.6% show uneven conversion. Water and environment is 23.3x against a 17.8x median, although its 0.05 EUR per-share contribution makes the effect on the share price immaterial. The market reading is therefore most sensitive to Electrical systems' thin profit base and the ability of acquired industrial businesses to turn sales into operating profit.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The first company-wide test is whether 2026 sales reach EUR 267m after EUR 126m in the first half. About EUR 9m of adjusted operating profit in the second half would complete analysts' EUR 13m forecast, compared with about EUR 4m in the first half. A shortfall would reduce the profit base behind every business allocation. Electrical systems requires outside sales of EUR 194m in 2028 versus EUR 129.7m in 2025, so order intake, backlog and delivered margins are the key evidence. A backlog of EUR 121.5m supports work volume, but competitive pricing could reduce its profit contribution toward a 4% margin. Industrial products and services needs EUR 86m of 2028 sales versus EUR 57.3m in 2025, with an 8% margin that must become steadier after the 2.9% and 14.6% quarterly outcomes. Labko's expected closing by the end of 2026, Coating Source's expected November closing and BRIX Facades' acquisition create integration tests. Water and environment needs sales near EUR 25m to arrive with a margin above zero; otherwise its 23.3x multiple remains based on almost no operating profit. These events determine what the current share price is made of in practice.

risks: Project-margin compression (Electrical systems): poorly priced or delayed contracts could leave the EUR 121.5m backlog adding sales without proportionate profit, with the operating margin as the early warning.

Forecast shortfall (all businesses): 2026 sales below EUR 267m or second-half adjusted operating profit below EUR 9m would reduce the forecast profit base, with quarterly sales and operating profit as the early warning.

Acquisition execution (Industrial products and services): Labko, Coating Source and BRIX Facades may add revenue without comparable profit, with segment margin after each closing as the early warning.

Public-sector pricing pressure (Water and environment): equipment deliveries could keep the segment near its 2025 adjusted loss despite EUR 25m forecast 2028 sales, with adjusted segment profit as the early warning.

Uneven trading (Industrial products and services): quarterly adjusted EBITA margins of 2.9% and 14.6% show that delivery reliability and efficiency can materially change profit, with the next quarterly margin as the early warning.
catalysts: 2026 results (near-term, all businesses): about EUR 9m of second-half adjusted operating profit would complete analysts' EUR 13m full-year forecast.

Backlog conversion (near-term, Electrical systems): delivery of the EUR 121.5m backlog at margins near the 6.8% adjusted pro forma EBITA level would support the EUR 10m 2028 operating-profit allocation.
Labko closing (near-term, Industrial products and services or Water and environment): completion by the end of 2026 with profitable sales would increase the relevant business's operating profit.
Coating Source closing (near-term, Industrial products and services): the expected November 2026 completion would test whether acquired EUR 6m 2025 revenue arrives with an adequate margin.
Margin improvement (medium-term, Water and environment): sales near EUR 25m with a margin above zero would move the near-zero profit base toward the listed peer comparison.

faqs.q: What is Auroora Yhtiöt Oyj's share price made of?
faqs.a: At 9.84 EUR per share, Electrical systems accounts for 8.90 EUR, Industrial products and services for 2.90 EUR and Water and environment for 0.05 EUR. The businesses total 11.85 EUR per share before debt and other claims, less cash of 2.01 EUR per share.

faqs.q: Why does Auroora trade above its listed peers?
faqs.a: The whole company trades at 20x analysts' 2028 operating profit versus listed peers at about 14.5x. Electrical systems is the main difference at 25.6x versus a 17.4x peer median, supported by its EUR 121.5m backlog but exposed to its 5% forecast margin.

faqs.q: What do analysts forecast for Auroora's sales and profit?
faqs.a: Analysts forecast sales of EUR 267m and operating profit of EUR 13m in 2026, rising to sales of EUR 305m and operating profit of EUR 18m in 2028. Net earnings are forecast at EUR 6m in 2026 and EUR 13m in 2028.

The key checks are 2026 sales of EUR 267m, second-half adjusted operating profit of about EUR 9m, Electrical systems backlog conversion and margins, Industrial products and services' quarterly margin, and the closings of Labko and Coating Source.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum's market report work?
faqs.a: The method keeps analysts' forecasts unchanged, splits forecast operating profit between businesses using reported segment results, compares each business with listed peers using EV/EBIT, and reads today's 9.84 EUR share price back into the businesses after debt and other claims, less cash.
